state:
Goal `core-test-1-2`, stage 2. Eleven of the twelve members the dossier check names have every
proof: `advance`, `answerHttp`, `answerSocket`, `assertCalled`, `assertNeverCalled`,
`assertEquals`, `assertEqualsDeep`, `assertCount`, `assertContains`, `assertDoesNotThrow` and
`assertCompletes`. Each Rust `covers:` test is in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs`'s tests module.
`assertCompletes` and `advance` carry a `perf` skip in `data/proofs/policy.json`: a bench runs
under `nvs run`, where no clock is fixed.

The one member still owed is `assertMatchesInline`: about, examples, hostile, perf and tests
(`bun nv proofs --id 'Core\Test::assertMatchesInline'`). It needs no fixed clock, so it runs at
the top level under `nvs run` and `bun nv try <files>` runs it. A bench needs
`bun nv proofs --record-perf --only '<member>'`. A member that only works inside
`#[Test(at: ...)]` is shown the way `docs/examples/core/Test/assertCompletes/` does: a `#[Test]`
class for the use, and top-level lines that print.

A Rust test of a failing assertion reads its sentence with `ctx.take_pending()`;
`assert_count_bounds_the_count_and_assert_contains_finds_across_the_numeric_row` is the shape for
plain values, and `assert_does_not_throw_and_assert_completes_judge_a_body_by_how_it_ended` for a
`callable` built in Rust.

Then run the whole `dossier-core-test-1-2` check and close any red line it prints. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`, `rule:testing/inline-snapshots`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs:3035`

backlog: `assertDoesNotThrow` quotes a thrown message whole: a message of ten million characters gives a failure message of the same length, while `assertEquals` shows only the start of a long value (`tests/hostile/core/Test/assertDoesNotThrow/01-bodies-that-throw-in-every-way.nvs`, step 2). The runtime survives; whether to shorten it is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/test.rs`'s call.
